title: Compiled component types still need resolvable script assets
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: This does not forbid multiple ordinary C# types per file or establish all Unity serialization cases. The evidence is the tested scene-generation path.
goal: Generate playable scenes using newly compiled component types.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Successful C# compilation was treated as sufficient for serialized component resolution.
what_worked: Historical correction: Split serializable component types into matching files and regenerate scenes through their source builder. Verification reported by the source: Three regenerated scenes had zero missing scripts, broken prefabs or other validation issues; final console and Windows build checks were clean.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Scene loading reported Unknown Behaviour after several public MonoBehaviour types were initially placed in one source file.
why: Confirmed for the observed generated-scene path: component definitions did not align with Unity's script-asset resolution boundary.
improved_method: Verify serialized scene reload and component references after code generation. Keep component file/script-asset identity coherent with generated scene references.
when_to_use: This does not forbid multiple ordinary C# types per file or establish all Unity serialization cases. The evidence is the tested scene-generation path.
when_not_to_use: This does not forbid multiple ordinary C# types per file or establish all Unity serialization cases.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
